title: The Dry Tree
journal: Dralin Uveran told me that Vosh-Leera, the root-herald of Jal-Veesa, who had me freed, will have work for me if I bring her some Sithis' beard, a grey moss hanging over the creek below Reed-Sill Weir. Crocodiles lie under the weir; he said I can kill them, shoot them from the log walk on top of the weir, or keep out of their sight, and if they see me they will come for me. First I need to pick the moss.
objectives: Pick Sithis' beard below Reed-Sill Weir. (marker: Sithis' Beard)

plan.going: I am free; Vosh-Leera of Jal-Veesa had me freed, and she will have work for me if I bring her Sithis' beard.
plan.next: Pick Sithis' beard below Reed-Sill Weir, then take it to Vosh-Leera in Jal-Veesa.
plan.ways: Fight the crocodiles, shoot them from the log walk, or sneak to the moss behind them.

answers: Vosh-Leera, root-herald of Jal-Veesa, had me freed from Dralin Uveran. She wants me at her house in Jal-Veesa, and I do not know why. Dralin says she will have work for me if I bring her Sithis beard, a grey moss below Reed-Sill Weir.
Pick the Sithis beard at the marker below Reed-Sill Weir, then go on to Jal-Veesa.
Kill the young crocodiles, shoot them from the log walk on the weir, or sneak past them unseen.
I do not understand what Hist means, or why Vosh-Leera wants me. I could ask people in Jal-Veesa.

title: The Dry Tree
journal: Vosh-Leera greeted me in her house. She is the root-herald of Jal-Veesa, who speaks for the town's elders and its tree to outsiders, and she had my name struck from the roll. The moss is not for her: the town's tree-minder, Weeltul, needs it for the sick Hist. Vosh-Leera asked me to take it to Weeltul at the Hist pool in the middle of the town, the tall grey tree standing in the water, and come back to her after.
objectives: Bring Sithis' beard to Weeltul at Jal-Veesa's Hist pool. (marker: Weeltul)

plan.going: Vosh-Leera, root-herald of Jal-Veesa, freed me. She gives work only to one who helps the tree-minder first; the moss is for the town's sick Hist. A Hist is a great thinking tree; Jal-Veesa's stands in the pool in the middle of the town.
plan.next: Bring the moss to Weeltul, the tree-minder, at the Hist pool, then go back to Vosh-Leera.
plan.ways: One way, handing it to her.

answers: Vosh-Leera is the root-herald who speaks for the town elders and tree to outsiders. The moss is for the tree-minder Weeltul, to warm the egg-pool of the sick Hist, the tall grey tree in the town pool. She will say why she freed me after I help Weeltul.
Take the moss to Weeltul at the Hist pool, let her show me the tree, then return to Vosh-Leera.
No real choice seen; just do it.
I still do not know exactly why she freed me, or what the egg-pool is. I can ask Weeltul.

title: The Dry Tree
journal: I gave the moss to Weeltul, the tree-minder of Jal-Veesa. The town's Hist is sick: its bark is dry and dark, its scar has closed and its egg-pool is cooling, and nobody knows why. If it dies, no egg here will hatch again. The moss only warms the pool. She let me lay a hand on the bark for its blessing, and told me Vosh-Leera is waiting for me in her house. I should go back to her.
objectives: Speak to Vosh-Leera in her house in Jal-Veesa. (marker: Vosh-Leera)

plan.going: Jal-Veesa's tree is sick (dry dark bark, a closed scar, a cooling egg-pool) for no known reason; if it dies the town's eggs never hatch. I have its blessing for a time.
plan.next: Go to Vosh-Leera's House and speak to her.

answers: Jal-Veesa Hist is dying: dry dark bark, closed scar, cooling egg-pool. If it dies no eggs hatch and the town empties. The moss only warms the pool. Weeltul gave me the tree blessing.
Return to Vosh-Leera in her house in Jal-Veesa to learn what I was freed for.
No choice yet; I could also ask Weeltul about the sap, scar, eggs and Umbriel first.
I do not know what caused the sickness, what the sap or scar means in detail, or what Umbriel was. I can ask Weeltul.

title: The Dry Tree
journal: Vosh-Leera told me who I work for now: the Toh-Reel-Ka, the "Secret Warriors" of the Xeech-Leel, who rule the province. They were made after Umbriel, when the An-Xileel used Lilmoth's mad tree to call a flying city down on the marsh, so that no tree and nobody allied with a tree can do it again. They free strangers like me because we come cheap and have no kin. She paid me fifty gold, and she has a second task for me: she asked me to come back to her here, in her house, for it.

plan.going: I work for the Toh-Reel-Ka, the secret order of the Xeech-Leel who rule the province, made to stop another Umbriel. I was freed because a stranger with no kin is a cheap spy. The trees are sick.
plan.next: Ask Vosh-Leera for her second task, here in her house (MN03 stage 10).

answers: I now work for the Toh-Reel-Ka, the Secret Warriors of the Xeech-Leel who rule the marsh. Trees are falling sick along the river and they want to know why. I was chosen as a kinless stranger, a cheap spy. I got 50 gold.
Come back to Vosh-Leera in her house for a second task.
Take the second task, or leave; I see no other stated option.
I do not know the cause of the sick trees, nor what the second task is. I can ask Vosh-Leera.
